perspective:
Ethan’s available information:

- Ethan knows he and Gary are long-time friends who met in middle school; Gary is a doctor.
- Ethan has noticed Gary working excessively long hours at the hospital, often skipping meals and sacrificing sleep, and he is concerned about Gary’s health.
- Ethan invited Gary to a two-day weekend retreat for relaxation/rejuvenation. He heard Gary initially decline, saying he appreciated the concern but had too much to do at the hospital.
- At the retreat, Ethan observed Gary acting restless and avoiding discussions about work. Ethan suspected Gary’s overworking had a deeper cause beyond professional obligations.
- Ethan confronted Gary, telling him they had been friends since middle school, that Gary could tell him anything, and that he was there to help, not judge. Gary replied that it was complicated and he didn’t want to burden Ethan.
- Gary then opened up to Ethan about the pressures of managing a new department and personal challenges he was facing. Ethan felt relief and empathy.
- Ethan suggested prioritizing tasks and delegating some responsibilities. Gary agreed and said he could use help organizing his schedule to make time for himself.
- Over the following months, Ethan regularly checked in with Gary about his progress and remaining challenges. Gary told him things were better, thanked him for his help, said he was less overwhelmed, and mentioned having time for a movie the previous weekend. Ethan felt hopeful and proud.
- After a year, Ethan saw Gary managing on his own with a healthier balance. Ethan felt satisfied and happy for him and decided to step back.
- Ethan told Gary he was always a call away and knew Gary had this. Gary thanked him, said he couldn’t have done it without Ethan’s support, and said he felt more in control.
